rules.label: React and Next runtime
rules.note: react + react-dom. Moves only on a Next or React upgrade.

rules.label: Next client runtime
rules.note: Router and hydration. Moves only on a Next upgrade.

rules.label: Shared app shell
rules.note: Mostly framer-motion, which every page pays for because _app wraps the tree in MotionConfig. The place to look first if this budget is ever the one that fails.

rules.label: Homepage route chunk
rules.note: The homepage's own components. The one chunk ordinary feature work actually grows.

rules.label: Legacy polyfills (nomodule)
rules.note: Shipped with the nomodule attribute, so no module-supporting browser requests it. Budgeted because it is deploy weight, and deliberately left out of the page critical-path totals because it is not visitor weight.

rules.label: All JavaScript
rules.note: Catches chunk proliferation, which the per-chunk budgets above cannot see: splitting one chunk into five keeps every per-chunk budget green.

rules.label: Stylesheet
rules.note: One render-blocking file: Tailwind's used utilities plus styles/globals.css. Tailwind purges against the content globs in tailwind.config.js, so this tracks classes actually referenced rather than the whole framework.

rules.label: Self-hosted fonts
rules.note: Nine files, but a visitor fetches two (62.6 kB: Inter latin and Lato latin), and those two are the only ones in the critical-path totals. next/font emits every subset Google returns and uses the `subsets` option to decide what to PRELOAD, not what to download, so the latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, greek-ext and vietnamese cuts ship unreferenced by any preload and are fetched only if a glyph in those ranges renders. There is no next/font option to stop emitting them.

rules.label: App icon
rules.note: Favicon and apple-touch-icon, referenced from the head in pages/_app.tsx.

rules.label: Schema logo
rules.note: 1551x1549, referenced only by the Organization structured data in lib/seo/site.ts, so crawlers fetch it and visitors never do. Large for what it is, but lib/seo/site.ts pins its dimensions and a unit test reads them back out of the PNG header, so re-encoding it is a change to make deliberately with that test in hand rather than as part of a size pass.

rules.label: Social card
rules.note: 1200x630, the standard OG card size. Fetched by crawlers and link unfurlers, not by visitors.

rules.label: Client logos
rules.note: Rendered by components/CompanyLogo.tsx. A sum rather than a per-file budget because the set grows as clients are added, and the total is what matters.
